# WHAT IS PRESENTATION SOFTWARE

## ULTIMATE GUIDE

In an era where effective communication is key, [**presentation software**](https://www.thedigideck.com/overview/) has become an essential tool for businesses, educators, and creatives alike. Whether you’re pitching a product, sending event guides, delivering a speech, or training a team, the right presentation software can help you convey your message in a clear, compelling, and memorable way.

Presentation platforms can also offer additional perks like asset management, analytics, collaboration, and more.

In this ultimate guide, we’ll explore what presentation software is, the different types available, their key use cases, and how to choose the right solution for your needs.

## What Is Presentation Software?

Presentation software is a tool or technology used to create slideshows that visually support spoken content. It allows users to combine text, images, graphics, and multimedia into a sequence of slides that can be projected on a screen or shared digitally. These programs are widely used in various settings, from classrooms and conferences to boardrooms and marketing pitches.

At its core, presentation software helps users organize information in a visually engaging format that enhances storytelling. It enables presenters to structure their content logically, add visual aids to emphasize key points, and keep their audience engaged.

![Presentation Software](https://cdn-ebaga.nitrocdn.com/pqcUOPQdSGWPxVJlJpEOWpkRdYCutflE/assets/images/optimized/rev-d4fd78e/thedigideck.wpenginepowered.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Presentation-Software-1024x540.jpg)

## Types of Presentation Software

Presentation software comes in various forms, each with unique features tailored to different needs. Here are the primary types:

![traditional slides presentation software](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

**Traditional Slide Deck Software**: These are the most common types of presentation software, featuring a slide-by-slide format where users can insert text, images, and basic animations. Examples include PowerPoint and Google Slides.

![interactive slides presentation software](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

**Interactive Presentation Platforms**: These go beyond the traditional static slides, offering interactive elements, multimedia integration, and advanced analytics to track viewer engagement. DIGIDECK is a top example in this category.

![collaborative slides presentation software](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

**Collaborative Presentation Tools**: Focused on teamwork, these platforms allow multiple users to collaborate in real-time on a presentation. Google Slides, DIGIDECK, and Prezi are popular tools in this space.

![](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

**AI-Powered Presentation Builders**: Leveraging artificial intelligence, these tools help users create visually appealing presentations with minimal effort. Beautiful.ai is a top player in this category.

## Use Cases for Presentation Software

Presentation software is versatile and can be used in various scenarios. Here are some common use cases:

- **Sales and Marketing Pitches**: Presentation software is essential for creating [persuasive sales decks](https://www.thedigideck.com/better-sales-presentations/) that showcase products and services, highlight key benefits, and close deals.
- **Educational Presentations**: [Teachers and educators](https://www.thedigideck.com/industries/education-presentation-software/) use presentation software to organize lessons, display key points, and incorporate multimedia to enhance learning.
- **Corporate Training**: Companies use presentations to onboard new employees, train staff on new processes, and ensure consistent messaging across departments.
- **Investor Pitches**: Entrepreneurs and startups rely on presentation software to create compelling pitch decks that communicate their business ideas, financial forecasts, and growth potential to potential investors.
- **Conferences and Keynotes**: Industry leaders and speakers use presentation software to create impactful visuals that support their speeches and engage large audiences.

## Benefits of a Presentation Platform

While traditional presentation software offers basic features, modern presentation platforms like DIGIDECK provide several advanced benefits:

- **Engaging Multimedia**: Incorporating videos, animations, and interactive elements can make presentations more dynamic and engaging.
- **Viewership Analytics**: With platforms like DIGIDECK, you can track how your audience interacts with your presentation, allowing for more informed follow-up and strategy adjustments.
- **Automation**: Presentation platforms can streamline the creation process by automating repetitive tasks, saving time, and ensuring consistency across presentations.
- **Customization**: Tailor your presentations to different audiences with [easy customization options](https://www.thedigideck.com/customize/), ensuring your message resonates with specific groups.
- **Cloud-Based Accessibility**: Modern presentation platforms are often cloud-based, allowing for easy access, sharing, and collaboration from anywhere.

![](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## 6 Top Presentation Software Solutions

There are many presentation tools on the market, each catering to different needs and preferences. Here are six top options:

![DIGIDECK by Sportsdigita](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

DIGIDECK is a cutting-edge presentation platform designed to create interactive, multimedia-rich presentations. It stands out with its powerful viewership analytics, which provide insights into who opened your presentation, when, and how long they viewed each slide for intentional, personalized follow-ups or for teachers and trainers to track participation.

With automation features, endless customization options, and robust CRM integrations, DIGIDECK is ideal for sales teams, marketers, and professionals looking to create compelling, data-driven presentations.

![Microsoft Office PowerPoint](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Microsoft PowerPoint is one of the most widely used presentation tools, known for its simplicity and familiar feature set. It offers a range of templates, design tools, and animations, making it a go-to option for users who need a reliable, traditional slide deck format.

![Prezi](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Prezi offers a more dynamic approach to presentations with its zoomable canvas format. Instead of linear slides, Prezi allows users to create presentations that flow seamlessly between topics, offering a more engaging and non-linear way to present information.

![beautiful ai](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Beautiful.ai leverages artificial intelligence to help users create aesthetically pleasing presentations quickly. It offers smart templates and design suggestions, making it an excellent choice for users who want to focus on content while ensuring their presentation looks professional and polished.

![google slides](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Google Slides is a cloud-based presentation tool that allows for real-time collaboration. It integrates with other Google Workspace apps and offers easy sharing options, making it popular for teams working together on presentations from different locations.

![keynote logo](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Keynote is Apple’s presentation software, known for its sleek design and powerful graphics capabilities. It’s a great option for Mac users who want to create appealing presentations with minimal effort.

## Choosing the Right Presentation Software

Selecting the right presentation software depends on your specific needs and goals. Here are a few factors to consider:

- **Functionality**: Do you need basic slide-building capabilities, or are you looking for advanced features like interactivity and analytics?
- **Ease of Use**: Consider how user-friendly the software is. Some platforms are familiar and intuitive while others have a steep learning curve.
- **Collaboration**: If your team works remotely or requires real-time collaboration, look for cloud-based options like Google Slides or DIGIDECK.
- **Customization**: Ensure the software allows you to customize your presentations to suit different audiences and purposes.
- **Analytics**: If you need insights into how your audience interacts with your presentation, choose a platform with viewership analytics.

## Ready for a Presentation Software That Goes to Work for You?

Presentation software is a valuable tool in today’s digital age for virtual and in-person presentations that need to make an impact. While some platforms like PowerPoint and Google Slides accomplish simple presentation needs, more robust tools like DIGIDECK are preferred for sales and marketing teams thanks to time-saving automations, viewership analytics, and CRM integrations.

DIGIDECK goes above and beyond a simple slide-by-slide presentation and allows your teams to collaborate remotely, customize for each prospect in just a few clicks, and saves hours each week with global update features, a centralized asset library, and pre-built slides.

Ready to see how the DIGIDECK presentation software can support your revenue efforts? [Request a demo today](https://www.thedigideck.com/demo-request-general/) to learn more.

Statements consisting only of original research should be removed._(September 2008)__([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance_template_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_ | _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance_template_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_ | [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/LibreOffice_7.2.4.1_Impress_screenshot.png/500px-LibreOffice_7.2.4.1_Impress_screenshot.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LibreOffice_7.2.4.1_Impress_screenshot.png) [LibreOffice Impress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LibreOffice_Impress "LibreOffice Impress"), one of the most popular [free and open-source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_and_open-source "Free and open-source") presentation programs In [computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computing "Computing"), a **presentation program** (also called **presentation software**) is a [software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software "Software") package used to display information in the form of a [slide show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slide_show "Slide show"). It has three major functions:[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-1) - an [editor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_editor "Text editor") that allows text to be inserted and [formatted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formatted_text "Formatted text") - a method for inserting and manipulating [graphic images](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_graphics "Computer graphics") and [media clips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_clip "Media clip") - a slide-show system to display the content Presentation software can be viewed\[ _[by whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_\] as enabling a functionally-specific category of [electronic media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_media "Electronic media"), with its own distinct culture and practices as compared to traditional presentation media (such as [blackboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackboard "Blackboard"), [whiteboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whiteboard "Whiteboard") and [flip charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_chart "Flip chart")). [Presentations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation "Presentation") in this mode of delivery have become pervasive in many aspects of [business communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_communication "Business communication"), especially in [business planning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_plan "Business plan"), as well as in [academic-conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_conference "Academic conference") and [professional conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_conference "Professional conference") settings, and in the [knowledge economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_economy "Knowledge economy") generally, where ideas are a primary work [output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Output_(economics) "Output (economics)"). Presentations may also feature prominently in political settings, especially in [workplace politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workplace_politics "Workplace politics"), where persuasion is a central determinant of group outcomes.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Most modern meeting-rooms and [conference halls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_hall "Conference hall") are configured to include presentation electronics, such as [projectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projector "Projector") suitable for displaying [presentation slides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_slide "Presentation slide"), often driven by the presenter's own [laptop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laptop "Laptop"), under direct control of the presentation program used to develop the presentation. Often a presenter will present a lecture using the slides as a visual aid both for the presenter (to track the lecture's coverage) and for the audience (especially when an audience member mishears or misunderstands the verbal component). Generally in presentations, the visual material is considered\[ _[by whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_\] supplemental to a strong aural presentation that accompanies the slide show, but in many cases, such as [statistical graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_graphics "Statistical graphics"), it can be difficult to convey essential information other than by visual means; additionally, a well-designed [infographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infographic "Infographic") can be extremely effective in a way that words are not. Endemic over-reliance on slides with low [information density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_design "Information design") and with a poor accompanying lecture has given presentation software a negative reputation as sometimes functioning as a crutch for the poorly informed or the poorly prepared. ## List of presentation programs Main article: [List of presentation programs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presentation_programs "List of presentation programs") ## History Using Autographix and [Dicomed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicomed "Dicomed"), it became quite easy\[ _[dubious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Accuracy_dispute#Disputed_statement "Wikipedia:Accuracy dispute")– [discuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Presentation_program#Dubious "Talk:Presentation program")_\] to make last-minute changes compared to traditional typesetting and pasteup. It was also a lot easier to produce a large number of slides in a small amount of time. However, these workstations also required skilled operators, and a single workstation represented an investment of $50,000 to $200,000 (in 1979 dollars). In the mid-1980s developments in the world of computers changed the way presentations were created. Inexpensive, specialized applications now made it possible for anyone with a PC to create professional-looking presentation graphics. Originally these programs were used to generate 35mm slides, to be presented using a [slide projector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slide_projector "Slide projector"). As these programs became more common in the late 1980s several companies set up services[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-meilach19870817-2) that would accept the shows on [diskette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diskette "Diskette") and create slides using a [film recorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_recorder "Film recorder") or print [transparencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transparency_(projection) "Transparency (projection)"). In the 1990s dedicated [LCD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_crystal_display "Liquid crystal display")-based screens that could be placed on the projectors started to replace the transparencies, and by the early 2000s they had almost all been replaced by [video projectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_projector "Video projector").\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] The first commercial computer software specifically intended for creating [WYSIWYG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WYSIWYG "WYSIWYG") presentations was developed at [Hewlett-Packard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard") in 1979 and called [BRUNO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRUNO_(software) "BRUNO (software)") and later HP-Draw. The first microcomputer-based presentation software was Cromemco's Slidemaster, developed by [John F. Dunn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Dunn "John F. Dunn") and released by [Cromemco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cromemco "Cromemco") in 1981.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-5) The first software displaying a presentation on a personal computer screen was [VCN ExecuVision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VCN_ExecuVision "VCN ExecuVision"), developed in 1982. This program allowed users to choose from a library of images to accompany the text of their presentation. [Harvard Graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Graphics "Harvard Graphics") was introduced for [MS-DOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MS-DOS "MS-DOS") and [Lotus Freelance Graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM_Lotus_Freelance_Graphics "IBM Lotus Freelance Graphics") was introduced for DOS and [OS/2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OS/2 "OS/2") in 1986. [PowerPoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerPoint "PowerPoint") was introduced for the [Macintosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_(computer) "Mac (computer)") computer in 1987.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-6) The first web-based presentation program was called ThinkFree Show, it launched in 2001 as part of the [ThinkFree Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ThinkFree_Office "ThinkFree Office") suite.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-7) Another web-based presentation program called Google Docs Presentations was introduced a few years later in 2007, it later became [Google Slides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Slides "Google Slides").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-8) ## Features A presentation program is supposed to help both the speaker with an easier access to their ideas and the participants with visual information which complements the talk. There are many different types of presentations including professional (work-related), education, entertainment, and for general communication. Presentation programs can either supplement or replace the use of older visual-aid technology, such as [pamphlets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamphlet "Pamphlet"), handouts, chalkboards, flip charts, posters, slides and overhead transparencies. Text, graphics, movies, and other objects are positioned on individual pages or "slides" or "foils"\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]. The "slide" analogy is a reference to the [slide projector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slide_projector "Slide projector"), a device that has become somewhat [obsolete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obsolescence "Obsolescence") due to the use of presentation software. Slides can be printed, or (more usually) displayed on-screen and navigated through at the command of the presenter. An entire presentation can be saved in video format.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-9) The slides can also be saved as images of any [image file formats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_file_formats "Image file formats") for any future reference.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-10) Transitions between slides can be animated in a variety of ways, as can the emergence of elements on a slide itself. Typically a presentation has many constraints and the most important being the limited time to present consistent information. Many presentation programs come with pre-designed images ( [clip art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clip_art "Clip art")) and/or have the ability to import graphic images. Some tools also have the ability to search and import images from [Flickr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flickr "Flickr") or [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") directly from the tool. Custom graphics can also be created in other programs such as [Adobe Photoshop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Photoshop "Adobe Photoshop") or [GIMP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GIMP "GIMP") and then exported. The concept of [clip art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clip_art "Clip art") originated with the image library that came as a complement with [VCN ExecuVision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VCN_ExecuVision "VCN ExecuVision"), beginning in 1983. With the growth of [digital photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_photography "Digital photography") and [video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_video "Digital video"), many programs that handle these types of media also include presentation functions for displaying them in a similar "slide show" format, for example [iPhoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhoto "IPhoto"). These programs allow groups of digital photos to be displayed in a slide show with options such as selecting transitions, choosing whether or not the show stops at the end or continues to loop, and including music to accompany the photos. Similar to programming [extensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_extension "Software extension") for an [operating system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system") or [web browser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_browser "Web browser"), "add ons" or [plugins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plug-in_(computing) "Plug-in (computing)") for presentation programs can be used to enhance their capabilities. Apps can enable a smartphone to be a remote control[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-11) for slideshow presentations, including slide previews, speaker notes, timer, stop watch, pointer, going directly to a given slide, blank screen and more. Presentation programs also offer an interactive integrated hardware element designed to engage an audience (e.g. [audience response systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audience_response "Audience response"), [second screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_screen "Second screen") applications) or facilitate presentations across different geographical locations through the internet (e.g. [web conferencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_conferencing "Web conferencing")).[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-12) Hardware devices such as [laser pointers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_pointer "Laser pointer") and [interactive whiteboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interactive_whiteboard "Interactive whiteboard") can ease the job of a live presenter . ### Programs As of 2007, MS [PowerPoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerPoint "PowerPoint") has become the dominant presentation tool because it is both readily available and easy for instructors to use (Grabe & Grabe 2007).[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-13) It allows instructors to create and manipulate presentations in a wide variety of contexts that can enhance student’s interest and engagement (Mills & Roblyer, 2006).[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-14) In addition, it helps instructors clearly identify the main points of a topic or activity while still providing the details through presentation (Loisel & Galer, 2004).[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_program#cite_note-15) Instructors can incorporate multiple types of media formats (e.g., diagram, photo, drawing, sound and video) that cannot be easily integrated together into one single medium. PowerPoint also provides graphical, transactional, aesthetic and interactive features. PowerPoint is for use in the classroom, and needs to be paired with use of an [LCD projector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LCD_projector "LCD projector") and large screen. ## See also - [Office suite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_suite "Office suite") - [Productivity software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Productivity_software "Productivity software") - [Wireless clicker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wireless_clicker "Wireless clicker") ## References 01. In computing, a presentation program is a software package used to display information in the form of a slide show. It has three major functions:
  - an editor that allows text to be inserted and formatted
  - a method for inserting and manipulating graphic images and media clips
  - a slide-show system to display the content Presentation software can be viewed as enabling a functionally-specific category of electronic media, with its own distinct culture and practices as compared to traditional presentation media. Presentations in this mode of delivery have become pervasive in many aspects of business communication, especially in business planning, as well as in academic-conference and professional conference settings, and in the knowledge economy generally, where ideas are a primary work output. Presentations may also feature prominently in political settings, especially in workplace politics, where persuasion is a central determinant of group outcomes. Most modern meeting-rooms and conference halls are configured to include presentation electronics, such as projectors suitable for displaying presentation slides, often driven by the presenter's own laptop, under direct control of the presentation program used to develop the presentation. Often a presenter will present a lecture using the slides as a visual aid both for the presenter and for the audience. Generally in presentations, the visual material is considered supplemental to a strong aural presentation that accompanies the slide show, but in many cases, such as statistical graphics, it can be difficult to convey essential information other than by visual means; additionally, a well-designed infographic can be extremely effective in a way that words are not. Endemic over-reliance on slides with low information density and with a poor accompanying lecture has given presentation software a negative reputation as sometimes functioning as a crutch for the poorly informed or the poorly prepared.

# Online presentation tools and software

Create inspiring presentations from customizable templates on any device, no matter where you are.

[Learn more](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/powerpoint) [Open PowerPoint](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2313327&clcid=0x409&culture=en-us&country=us)

![A person sitting on a chair working on his laptop](https://cdn-dynmedia-1.microsoft.com/is/image/microsoftcorp/356987-hero-main?resMode=sharp2&op_usm=1.5,0.65,15,0&wid=360&hei=250&qlt=100&fit=crop)

## What is presentation software?

Presentation software allows you to create visually engaging slideshows with text, images, charts, and multimedia elements. Structure information in a compelling way, whether you’re delivering a pitch, teaching a class, or sharing project updates.

### How to use presentation software

#### Get started

Create an account or sign in to your presentation software platform. Most presentation maker tools offer web-based access, so you can work from any device.

#### Choose a template

Browse a [template library](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2266022) and select one that aligns with your content. Customize fonts, colors, and layouts to match your brand.

#### Add content

1. **Slides**: Start adding slides. Each slide represents a topic or point you want to cover.

2. **Text**: Keep text short and concise, use bullet points, and keep the font size large for easy viewing and skimming.

3. **Graphics**: Insert relevant images, charts, and icons. Visuals enhance understanding.

4. **Multimedia**: Embed video and audio elements directly into your slides.

#### Collaborate with team members

1. **Invite collaborators:** [Share the presentation](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2283631) with your team members by sending them a link or inviting them directly through the software.

2. **Work together in real time:** Once your team members have access, they can start editing the slide presentation simultaneously. Use the built-in chat and comment features to communicate and provide feedback in real time.

3. **[Track changes](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2283632) and maintain version history:** Keep track of all edits made by team members. If needed, you can revert to previous versions of the presentation.

#### Save and export

1. **Save regularly:** Save your work frequently to avoid losing progress. Most software offers an auto-save feature to help with this.

2. **Choose the best export option:** Export your presentation as a PDF, PowerPoint file, or shareable link. Choose a format that works best for your audience.

3. **Select appropriate export settings:** Choose the quality and format that best suits your purpose. For example, if you're sharing the presentation online, you might choose a lower resolution to reduce file size, whereas for a high-quality print, a higher resolution would be more appropriate.

### Presentation software features

#### Customizable templates

The right template can make your content pop. [Template libraries](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2266022) include options that work for a range of different scenarios, from business presentations and financial reports to lesson plans and creative endeavors. Customize layouts, fonts, and colors to match your brand identity.

#### Real-time collaboration

Collaborate seamlessly with colleagues, no matter where they are. Edit presentation slides together, leave comments, and see changes in real time.

#### Multimedia integration

Embed videos, images, and audio files directly into your slides. Visuals and multimedia enhance engagement and convey complex ideas effectively.

#### Cloud storage and access

Access your presentations from any device without worrying about lost files or compatibility issues.

#### AI-powered tools

Streamline tasks and busywork with new [AI features,](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/word/ai-writing) like those available via [Microsoft Copilot](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2279878). Ask Copilot to draft presentations, suggest slide content, and help with design—all with your organization’s branding.

#### Export and sharing options

Share your slide presentation effortlessly. Export to different formats or generate a shareable link. Collaborators and clients can view your work, offer feedback, and make edits.

### Presentation software benefits

#### Create presentations easily

Customizable templates and intuitive design tools allow you to craft professional presentations with ease. Whether for a corporate setting or a personal project, these tools provide a variety of options to suit any theme or topic, making sure that your presentation stands out.

#### Collaborate seamlessly

Presentation makers offer features that allow multiple users to work on the same presentation simultaneously, regardless of their location. Teams can work together efficiently, combining their expertise to produce a cohesive final product.

#### Access from any device

Help your team be more productive by giving them the flexibility to access and edit presentations from any device. Whether you're using a desktop at the office, a laptop at home, or a tablet while traveling, your work is available at your fingertips, ready to be polished or presented.

### Presentation tool use cases

#### Business presentations and proposals

Creating slides that incorporate data, visuals, and narratives can help communicate your business project or idea more effectively.

_Example:_ Drafting a proposal for a potential client, a business associate can use a presentation tool to incorporate market analysis, projected figures, and testimonials into slides, making a strong case for the proposal.

#### Educational lectures and workshops

Create engaging content for educational lectures and workshops that enhances the learning experience with interactive elements.

_Example_: Designing an interactive workshop presentation on climate change, an educator can use the presentation tool to include interactive graphs, videos, and quizzes to engage the audience and facilitate learning.

#### Marketing and sales

Presentation tools help create impactful materials that highlight the benefits of products or services, driving sales and engagement.

_Example:_ Developing a sales pitch deck for a new product launch, a marketer can use the tool to showcase product features, customer testimonials, and competitive analysis to persuade potential buyers.

#### Creative and personal projects

Presentation makers aren't just for business—they're also perfect for personal and creative projects like photo slideshows for special events, design portfolios, or travel journals.

_Example:_ Creating a photo slide presentation for a family reunion, a family member can use presentation software to compile memorable photos, add music, and include captions to share cherished moments with loved ones.

### Tips and best practices

#### Make a strategic plan

Outline your main message and supporting points to maintain focus and help ensure that your slide presentation flows logically.

_Example:_ For a business presentation introducing a new product offering, create a main message like: "Our latest innovation sets a new standard in its category." Outline supporting points that detail unique attributes differentiating the product from competitors, offering evidence of its benefits, and quoting positive feedback from early adopters.

#### Design for your audience

Consider the needs and expectations of your audience. Use language, visuals, and [data](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/excel/data-analysis) that resonate with them and reinforce your message.

_Example_: For a report to a group of healthcare professionals, design a slide presentation on medical equipment that uses technical language they’re familiar with, along with visuals like diagrams of the equipment and data on its efficacy.

#### Keep it simple and visual

Avoid cluttering presentation slides with too much text. Use visuals like images, charts, and infographics to illustrate your points and keep the audience engaged.

_Example_: For a presentation about social media trends, instead of paragraphs of text, use infographics to represent statistical data and icons to symbolize different social media platforms.

#### Be consistent

Maintain a consistent design throughout your presentation. Use the same fonts, colors, and styles to create a cohesive look and feel.

_Example:_ For a series of business presentations on financial literacy, use a consistent color scheme that reflects your brand, the same font style for headings and body text, and a standard layout for each slide.

#### Engage with storytelling

Incorporate storytelling elements to make your presentation more relatable and memorable. Use concrete examples, anecdotes, or case studies to illustrate your points.

_Example:_ For a presentation about renewable energy, share a story about a community that transitioned to solar power, detailing the challenges they faced, the solutions they implemented, and the positive impact on their lives.

#### Make it interactive

Take advantage of the advanced features of your presentation tool. Use animations to highlight key points, and interactive elements to engage your audience and make your content more dynamic.

_Example:_ For a presentation on a new software tool, use the presentation maker’s interactive features to demonstrate the software live, allowing the audience to see its functionality in real time. Animate slide transitions to reflect the narrative progression. For instance, use a fade transition to signify a smooth transition from one topic to the next, or a dynamic wipe to indicate a significant shift in topic.

#### Take advantage of AI features

Some [presentation apps come equipped with AI features](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/powerpoint/ai-powerpoint-generator) that can suggest design improvements, offer content ideas, and even generate slides based on your input.

_Example_: For a training module, utilize AI-powered design suggestions to optimize the layout of your slides. Let AI analyze the content of each slide and recommend design enhancements, such as aligning text for better readability or suggesting visuals that complement your message.

#### Match content to the template

A vast library of templates provides a starting point for any presentation, whether it's corporate, educational, or personal. Select a template that complements and enhances your content to help ensure clarity, engagement, and cohesiveness.

_Example:_ For a startup pitch, select a template that embodies a modern, innovative feel that provides a structured flow for introducing your team, showcasing your product, detailing the market opportunity, and concluding with your business model and ask.

#### Gather input from others

Team members can work on the same presentation from different locations, chat within the tool, and track changes in real time, making collaboration effortless and transparent.

_Example_: For a cross-departmental project launch, use the collaboration features to allow team members from marketing, product development, and sales to contribute to the presentation. They can add slides, provide feedback, and make edits, ensuring that the final presentation is representative of all departments involved.

Walk into any meeting room, classroom, or virtual conference today, and you’ll see the same thing: someone presenting ideas visually. Whether it’s a startup pitch, quarterly report, or training session, presentations have become one of the primary ways professionals communicate. But behind every strong presentation is the same foundation, a tool designed to turn ideas into something people can see, follow, and remember.

So what is presentation software, really? And why does it matter more now than ever?

This guide breaks down the presentation software meaning, explains what a [presentation](https://www.paperpapers.com/news/digital-notes-vs-paper-notes/) is, and shows you how to create one that holds attention instead of losing it.

Table of Contents

[Toggle](https://www.paperpapers.com/news/what-is-presentation-software/#)

## **What Is a Presentation?**

Before we talk about software, we need to define the core concept.

A presentation is a structured way of communicating information to an audience using visuals, spoken explanation, and supporting media. It’s not just information, it’s information organized for clarity and impact.

At its best, a presentation does three things:

- Explains ideas clearly
- Guides attention intentionally
- Makes information memorable

Presentations show up everywhere: sales meetings, lectures, investor briefings, training sessions, conferences. The format varies, but the goal is consistent—help people understand something they didn’t understand before.

Historically, presenters relied on printed charts or overhead projectors. Today, digital tools do the heavy lifting, making it easier to organize ideas visually and deliver them with confidence.

## **What Is Presentation Software? Meaning and Definition**

Let’s answer the central question: what is presentation software?

Presentation software is a digital tool that allows users to create visual content, text, images, charts, video, graphics, and display it in a structured format for an audience. In practical terms, it’s a [presentation](https://prezi.com/) [creation platform](https://prezi.com/) designed to turn raw ideas into clear visual communication.

Most presentation tools include features that let you:

- Arrange information
- Design visual layouts
- Add multimedia elements
- Present live or share remotely

Traditional software was dependent on a slide-by-slide approach. Modern platforms have expanded that model, giving presenters more flexible ways to organize information and guide viewers through ideas.

## **Why Presentation Software Matters More Than Ever**

Presentations aren’t just helpful anymore, they’re essential.

Attention is harder to keep. Audiences skim through information instead of listening. In this environment, how it is presented can determine whether it sticks or fades away.

Research in educational psychology shows that people understand and retain information better when visuals and spoken explanations work together. In other words, strong visuals don’t just look good—they improve comprehension.

That’s why professionals increasingly rely on an [online presentation tool](https://prezi.com/) that does more than display bullet points. The best platforms help presenters guide attention, show relationships between ideas, and keep audiences engaged from start to finish.

## **Static Slides vs. Presentations That Move**

Not all presentation software is built the same way, and the difference shows up fast when you’re presenting.

Traditional slide decks follow a straight line: slide one, slide two, slide three. This works for simple reporting, but it can feel rigid, especially when explaining complex topics or big-picture ideas.

Newer formats use a canvas approach instead of stacked slides. This allows presenters to zoom in, zoom out, and move between ideas visually. Instead of flipping pages, you guide your audience through a landscape of information.

Movement isn’t decoration, it’s direction. It shows how ideas connect, which helps people follow your logic.

## **Features That Define Modern Presentation Software**

If you’re choosing a presentation creation platform, certain capabilities make a real difference.

**Visual design flexibility** lets you control layout, branding, fonts, and color so your presentation looks polished without requiring design expertise.

**Multimedia support** allows you to include charts, video, images, and graphics that reinforce your message.

**Collaboration tools** make it possible for teams to edit presentations together in real time, no matter where they’re located.

**AI-powered creation** is one of the biggest shifts. Instead of starting from a blank screen, you can generate a complete presentation from a document, outline, or prompt. That means less time formatting and more time refining ideas.

## **How to Create a Powerful Presentation**

Strong presentations start with strong thinking. Here’s a process that actually works and it doesn’t matter how many people you are presenting it to.

### **1\. Start With One Clear Idea**

Every effective presentation revolves around a single takeaway. If your audience remembers only one thing, what should it be?

Define that before opening any software.

### **2\. Build the Structure First**

Create your presentation as a story.

- Start with why this matters
- Move on to what they need to know
- End it with what they should do

Structure keeps your message focused and avoids information overload.

### **3\. Design for Understanding**

Avoid crowding visuals with text. Instead:

- Highlight key points
- Use visuals to reinforce meaning
- Show relationships between ideas

Design should clarify your message, not compete with it.

### **4\. Use AI to Move Faster**

Deadlines don’t wait for inspiration. AI tools can instantly generate layouts, organize content, and suggest visuals based on your topic.

### **5\. Guide Attention With Motion**

Movement should help your audience follow along. Smooth transitions, zooming, and visual pathways keep viewers oriented and focused.

When motion supports meaning, people stay engaged longer.

### **6\. Practice Delivery**

Even the best presentation won’t land if delivery feels uncertain. Rehearse your flow, refine transitions, and get comfortable navigating your visuals. Confidence is part of the presentation experience.

## **Common Presentation Mistakes**

Strong presenters avoid a few predictable pitfalls:

- Slides overloaded with text
- Reading directly from visuals
- Inconsistent design
- No clear narrative
- Treating presentations like documents instead of experiences

A presentation isn’t a report. It’s a guided conversation with your audience.

## **Where Presentation Software Is Headed**

Presentation tools are evolving quickly, and the trend is clear: they’re becoming smarter, faster, and more intuitive.

Expect continued growth in:

- AI-generated presentations
- Interactive storytelling formats
- Real-time collaboration
- Automatic design optimization
- Hybrid-friendly presenting tools

As communication shifts toward virtual and hybrid environments, presenters need tools that adapt just as quickly as their ideas do.

## **Why Prezi**

If you’re evaluating what presentation software should actually do for you, it comes down to three outcomes: clarity, speed, and confidence.

Prezi is designed around exactly those priorities.

**Presentations that move**

Zoomable visuals guide attention and show how ideas connect, making complex information easier to understand.

**Create fast**

Prezi AI turns ideas into structured presentations in seconds, helping you meet deadlines without sacrificing quality.

**Create with confidence**

Layouts, visuals, and flow are generated automatically, so you don’t need design experience to produce something polished.

The result is a presentation that feels intentional, engaging, and easy to follow—for both you and your audience.

## **Final Thoughts**

Understanding what presentation software isn’t just about definitions. It’s about recognizing how the right tool changes the [way ideas](https://www.paperpapers.com/news/so-youve-bought-paper-now-what-paper-ideas/ "Creative Paper Ideas – Fun & Unique Ways to Use Your Paper") are communicated.

Strong presentations don’t happen by accident. They happen when structure, visuals, and delivery work together.

And when your presentation holds attention, your message has a chance to do what it’s meant to do: move people.

## **Ready to Build a Presentation That Moves?**

If you want to create clear, engaging presentations without spending hours designing slides, it’s time to try a smarter approach.

Prezi helps you turn ideas into polished, dynamic presentations in seconds—so you can focus on your message, not formatting. Start creating presentations that move today.

# What is Presentation software?

## Presentation software Definition

Personal computer software that provides easy-to-use platforms for creating effective reports and presentations.

Presentation software refers to digital tools used to create and deliver visual displays of research findings. In marketing research, it helps communicate complex data, insights and recommendations in a clear and engaging way to clients and stakeholders.

### What are the key aspects of presentation software in marketing research?

- Supports visuals such as charts, graphs and infographics.
- Enables narrative flow through slides or decks.
- Allows integration of videos, animations and embedded data.
- Customizable design templates for branding consistency.
- Facilitates remote or live client presentations.

### Why is presentation software important in market research?

It allows researchers to distill and display insights in a digestible and persuasive manner, making it easier for decision makers to understand and act on the findings. It also ensures that key messages are delivered with clarity and visual impact.

### Who relies on presentation software in marketing research?

- Research analysts and consultants.
- Client services and account teams.
- Marketing and brand managers.
- Executives presenting insights to internal stakeholders.
- Design teams translating data into visuals.

### How do market researchers use presentation software?

Market researchers use presentation software – such as PowerPoint, Google Slides or Keynote – to transform data tables and qualitative findings into visually engaging reports. After analysis, researchers craft story-driven presentations that highlight key insights, support strategic recommendations and guide client decisions. Slides often include charts, word clouds, video clips and dynamic visuals that help simplify complex ideas and maintain audience engagement. Presentation software is also commonly used in debriefs, pitch meetings and webinars, providing a flexible platform for tailoring content to varied audiences, whether they’re boardroom executives or product development teams.

For Apple users, Keynote produces visually exceptional presentations with moderate learning curve. ### Are online presentation software secure for sensitive data? Professional solutions (Google Workspace Business, Microsoft 365 Business, Pitch Enterprise) offer encryption, access controls, and GDPR compliance. Free versions present more risks. For very sensitive data, favor on-premise installations or solutions with security certifications specific to your industry (ISO 27001, SOC 2). ### Can you collaborate on presentations between different software? Cross-platform collaboration remains limited. PPTX format serves as exchange standard but loses certain specific features during conversions. For smooth collaboration, the entire team must use the same tool. If impossible, define a reference format (generally PPTX) and accept import/export limitations. # What Is a Presentation Software and When Should You Use One

[![](https://mobisystems.com/sb-assets/f/294288/1333x2000/8e4503a1eb/reny-mihaylova.jpg)Reny Mihaylova](https://mobisystems.com/en-eu/blog/authors/reny-mihaylova)

Jan 28, 2025

![art direction image](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1920x1024%2F206cbdd60f%2Fwhat-is-a-presentation-software-and-when-should-you-use-one_.png&w=3832&q=100)

Your boss has just asked you to create a presentation to showcase a new product, deliver a compelling speech, or lead a team training.

But you’re aiming for more than the standard, “template-filled” look, and there's one small problem: you don’t have Microsoft PowerPoint installed.

Choosing the right presentation software can mean the difference between delivering an engaging, memorable pitch and falling short of your audience's expectations.

The right presentation tool enhances your message's clarity and ensures it sticks.

Are you new to presentation software or do you want to boost your productivity with something beyond PowerPoint? Well, you’re in the right place.

In this guide, you’ll learn how to choose the best [PowerPoint alternatives](https://mobisystems.com/en-eu/blog/industry-insights/powerpoint-alternatives-for-mac), packed with must-have features for fast, collaborative, and professional presentations.

## What is presentation software?

Presentation software, often called presentation programs or graphics applications, is designed to help users craft engaging, visual presentations.

Presentation tools organize content through slides, blending text, photos, and multimedia, guiding audiences via a narrative that supports your spoken words.

![MobiSlides interface with a new slide menu open, displaying various slide layout options on the left and a blank slide on the right.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1310x806%2Fa2c4a7c0c1%2F1.png&w=3832&q=100)

To insert a new slide, select "New" and the design from the templates.

Presentation tools go beyond just displaying information – they structure it logically and visually.

Whether you’re presenting complex data or a fresh idea, presentation software solutions allow you to make your key points memorable.

## What to use presentation software for?

Wondering how presentation software can cater to your unique needs, audience, or purpose?

Read on to learn how to integrate presentation apps throughout your professional life.

### Work

Presentation software supports a wide range of professional tasks, like:

- Creative briefs and mood boards.

- Pitch decks and proposals.

- Competitor analysis and market insights.

- Project reports and annual reviews.

- Marketing and strategic plans.

- Product demos.

- Client proposals.

- Sales and investor pitches.

- Conference keynotes.

- Training modules.


![A presentation slide featuring a network of illustrated business people connected by lines on a blue background. A menu is open on the left.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1368x926%2Fd676385398%2F2.png&w=3832&q=100)

Insert business presentation templates from "File">"New file from template..."

### University

A custom presentation provides a visual aid for students and educators, preparing:

- Lectures and class presentations.

- Research projects and group assignments.

- Workshops and seminars.

- Educational presentations.


![Template with a notebook and pencil image. Slide shows layout options and text placeholders for title, subtitle, instructor, and course.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1826x859%2Fc54b0ccbd0%2F3.png&w=3832&q=100)

Change your course presentation's design from the "Layout" function.

### School

Students benefit from using interactive presentations for:

- School projects and book reports.

- Science fairs, history projects, or group assignments.

- Art, writing, or personal interest projects.


![Green presentation slide with "Assignment Title," "Student name," and "Course Title | Course Number" in white text. Yellow bookmark design.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1862x798%2F484610a1fe%2F4.png&w=3832&q=100)

To delete a slide in your student assignment, right-click it from the menu on the left and select "Delete Slide."

## How to create presentations that work?

To create a successful presentation, you should plan; considering your purpose and audience, presentation design and narrative, and more.

### Plan and structure your content

Before opening any presentation apps, build a map to pinpoint what you want to cover and the presentation flow.

Start by identifying:

- Who you'll be talking to? Your audience’s familiarity with the subject will help you decide on the language and depth of information.

- What is your overarching message?

- What are your objectives: do you aim to inform, educate, or inspire?


To keep the flow consistent ensure each slide has a single key point that naturally leads up to a strong call to action.

![A blank table with four columns labeled: Audience, Main message, Presentation Objectives, and Call to action. Three empty rows are below.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1079x613%2F62b9719c8f%2F5.png&w=2560&q=100)

You can even create a slide that details all of this information ("Insert" > "Table").

### What's the story?

Your presentation narrative is the thread that ties everything together – your motivation for the presentation, your audience’s interests, and the unique insights you bring.

After clarifying the story, create a detailed outline as a guide for both speech and slides, ensuring no key elements are overlooked.

### Presentation design

When it comes to design, make the most of presentation software’s built-in tools to keep your slides visually appealing yet straightforward.

Utilize pre-built templates to maintain brand colors and consistency while adding customization as needed.

Keep multimedia elements relevant, high-quality, and purposeful to enhance your message.

The minimalistic design remains one of the best approaches for professional presentations. Simple and clean layouts maintain an elegant appearance and help audiences focus on the content.

![A presentation slide editor showing a blank slide with a sidebar displaying various design themes on the right.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1613x919%2F9678a069fa%2F6.png&w=3832&q=100)

Select "Design" > "Themes..." to find minimalistic, color-coordinated options.

### Speech o'clock

Although you’ll build some of your speech as you create your stunning presentations, dedicate extra time to shaping it fully.

Start by, once again, identifying the core reason you’re speaking to this audience.

Plan for a powerful opening and closing to leave a lasting impact.

Add your speaker notes to your presentation, they'll act as prompts to help you stay on track and avoid getting lost or stuck.

![Screenshot of a blank MobiSlides slide.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1325x861%2F26d76542aa%2F7.png&w=3832&q=100)

Type in your notes below your presentation slide.

### Practice makes perfect

Once you feel prepared, test the presentation software, technology, and timing of any multimedia elements.

Note how long your presentation takes – add any missing information and trim unnecessary elements to keep the message concise.

### Finalize your presentation

Set aside at least a day to ensure your slide decks are flawless.

Start by focusing on the design details – ensure images and text are aligned; colors are consistent; and correct any typos.

After this, rehearse your presentation from start to finish.

In a second round of review, focus on tone, grammar, and punctuation to refine your writing.

## What should every PowerPoint presentation have?

Presentation software provides a powerful suite of tools that not only make slide creation easy but also help you design presentations that are polished, brand-aligned, and captivating for any audience.

Here are the key features you need to look out for:

### Templates

Many platforms come with professionally designed presentation templates that make creating visually appealing presentations a breeze.

With drag-and-drop presentation templates, you can match your slides to company branding and even search a library of pre-approved layouts and designs for faster formatting.

![A grid of various presentation templates with titles like "Academic Presentation," "Brunch," and "Project Presentation" displayed.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1012x567%2F95a0b86d06%2F8.png&w=2560&q=100)

Here are samples of 17 built-in presentation templates.

### Color aesthetic

Colors carry psychological associations that can impact how messages are received, so your presentation colors should align with your brand’s message.

If you’re short on time, opt for PowerPoint templates that align with your branding colors to avoid unnecessary customization.

### Typeface and font size

The ideal typeface should be all systems-available, such as Arial or Calibri, ensuring compatibility on any device.

Limit yourself to a maximum of three typefaces per presentation to maintain a clean and cohesive look.

As for your title fonts, they should be between 36-44 pt, while body text should range from 24-28 pt. A single quote or key phrase on a dedicated slide can be effective, using a larger, 36 pt size in italics.

Bold text is ideal for emphasizing key concepts, while italics can highlight foreign terms or quotes.

Select your typeface and font size from the dedicated menu.

### Format

The standard 16:9 format offers a rectangular layout, widely compatible with modern devices and projectors, and prints well on A4 paper.

The 4:3 format's square layout can be more challenging for creating emphasis, but it ensures your presentation looks consistent on most projection equipment.

To change your format, go to "File"> "Page setup."

### Collaboration

Cloud-based software often includes shared workspaces, letting teams collaborate on presentations, provide feedback, and track real-time progress.

With version control, you can easily manage changes, access prior versions, and review contributions from team members.

Share your presentation with your team via the link sharing options.

### Stock libraries and visual assets access

Some presentation tools provide access to built-in libraries with images, photos, icons, and animations, while others integrate with sources like Unsplash or Giphy.

You can pull in high-quality visuals to strengthen your message and make your presentation even more dynamic.

Select "Insert" > "Image" > "Search the web" or "GIFS and stickers."

### Video, audio, and data integrations

Many programs support video embedding from sites like YouTube and offer audio integration, so you can add voiceovers or sound effects to bring slides to life.

Plus, some applications connect with data sources like Google Analytics or Sheets, letting you back up your story with real-time data insights.

From "Insert" > "Video" and search the clips you'd like to embed in your presentation.

### Animation options

Transitions are key for holding attention, with options to control speed and sequence.

Keep your animations simple, lightweight, and consistent, as they should move smoothly between slides rather than distracting the audience.

![A slide template with text placeholders for a title and subtitle, alongside transition effect options on the right panel.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1471x882%2F5d07876024%2F14.png&w=3832&q=100)

Select the transitions that'd best fit your presentation.

### Smart design tools

Advanced tools often include a built-in designer that automatically applies formatting rules, ensuring consistency without manual adjustments.

Features like automatic font resizing, color matching, and logo placement keep your presentations on-brand and polished.

## What Is the Best Presentation Software out There?

In the next section of this guide, we'll provide you with the [best presentation tools](https://mobisystems.com/en-eu/blog/industry-insights/the-best-presentation-software-in-2024) to suit your needs.

### MobiSlides

[MobiSlides](https://mobisystems.com/en-eu/mobioffice/mobislides) is an intuitive and powerful tool for creating and delivering eye-catching presentations, whether for a corporate keynote or a school project.

The presentation software provides easy options for building slides, from choosing themes and templates to diving into its rich editor to customize layouts with text, media, and effects.

![A slide displaying a shapes menu with various line and rectangle options on a blank canvas.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1636x750%2Fd27dad429f%2F15.png&w=3832&q=100)

To insert an object, select the shape you wish from the designed menu.

Meanwhile, its Slide Master tool allows you to customize multiple slides simultaneously.

Slides help users present confidently by allowing them to rehearse timings and use presenter view for a seamless delivery.

![A presentation screen with a pop-up window showing slideshow options, including slide timing and display settings.](https://mobisystems.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fa.storyblok.com%2Ff%2F294288%2F1007x871%2F1ccee07796%2F16.png&w=2560&q=100)

To fix your tming, go to "Slideshow" > "Slideshow Settings..."

MobiSheets' standout feature is its compatibility with other major presentation formats like PowerPoint and Keynote, making it a versatile choice for anyone needing to share their work across different devices or platforms.

### PowerPoint

Microsoft PowerPoint remains one of the most popular presentation software, known for its user-friendly design tools, multimedia integrations, and wide range of templates.

Here are some templates for your PowerPoint presentations.

PowerPoint’s simplicity and familiarity make it a go-to choice for users who want a reliable, traditional slide deck experience.

The presentation software offers rich design tools, animations, and an easy-to-use interface that’s accessible to all levels of presenters.

Edit your powerpoint slides' animations and transitions swiftly, from the designated menu above your presentation deck.

### Apple Keynote

Keynote, designed specifically for Apple users, is known for its high-quality graphics and ease of use.

Preloaded for free on Apple products, Keynote is a user-friendly tool offering sleek template layouts and stunning animations.

Choose your theme and presentation format, when you open the application.

Add your animations and effects from the right-hand side menu.

Keynotes provides seamless compatibility with macOS and iOS devices, making it especially convenient for those within the Apple ecosystem.

### Google Slides

Google Slides is a cloud-based presentation software, ideal for teams needing real-time collaboration.

Slides are accessible from any device with internet access, a valuable feature for teams working from different locations.

Google Slides allows multiple users to work on a presentation simultaneously, with changes saved automatically and accessible to all collaborators.

Check when your presentation was last edited and share it with your team.

With familiar design and layout options, users can quickly create or edit slides while also benefiting from Google’s robust sharing and collaboration features.

Change your layout from "Slide"> "Apply layout."

### WPS Presentation

WPS Presentation is a free, cross-platform presentation software that offers a user-friendly experience similar to PowerPoint.

Compatible with multiple file formats like .ppt and .pptx, WPS Presentation enables seamless sharing and editing across devices, from Windows PCs to iOS and Android.

The software boasts an extensive library of templates and design resources, empowering users to create professional presentations quickly.

Check out some of the templates for your future presentations from the menu.

Customize your presentations's design from the designated menu.

## Conclusion

Choose the right presentation software to create a polished, engaging presentation that resonates with your audience and meets your unique goals.

From corporate pitches to classroom presentations, these tools offer flexibility, collaboration, and impactful design features that take your ideas further.

Don’t settle for standard templates; explore the best presentation software that aligns with your message and enhances audience engagement.

Ready to upgrade your presentation skills? Try MobiSlides for free and start creating standout presentations today!

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How do you choose a presentation software?

Choosing the best presentation tools depends on your needs and goals.

Consider the platform's functionality: do you need a straightforward slide builder, or are advanced features like interactivity and analytics important?

Also, keep ease of use in mind – certain software is intuitive while others have a learning curve.

A user-friendly platform simplifies the presentation process, and by using the same tool consistently, you can automate brand elements like colors, fonts, and logos, creating a cohesive library of presentations.

Collaboration is also essential; if your team works remotely or requires real-time collaboration, opt for cloud-based software, which enables simultaneous edits, streamlined communication, and brand consistency across departments.

### What is better than PowerPoint?

Affordable alternatives like MobiSlides and Google Slides offer powerful tools, templates, and design features similar to PowerPoint but at a lower cost. These platforms are highly compatible with PowerPoint formats, making it easy to create impressive presentations without breaking the bank.

### Can you get PowerPoint for free?

Yes, you can use Microsoft PowerPoint for free by creating presentations online through your Microsoft Office account. This online version provides the essential features of PowerPoint, accessible from any device with internet access.

Over the last few years, I’ve moved to using [reveal.js](https://revealjs.com/#%2F "revealjs.com") to create slides for my talks.

I’m no graphic designer but I do know a bit of HTML and CSS and reveal.js makes it easy for me to achieve the polished, minimalist look I want without too much effort.

![](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-62bd43cff7dfbda9f19bab6d1aa34b63)

The title slide for [my talk about radix trees at Lambda World 2018](http://jelv.is/talks/lambda-world-2018/ "jelv.is").

The power of reveal.js lies, ironically, in how it is not powerful. You don’t work in a WYSIWYG¹ editor that lets you do anything; instead, you write a detailed outline that is compiled to your slideshow:

![](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-b3f5a274968cd13a203455716366ecc9-pjlq)

Here is an excerpt from the source for the same talk. You see a section slide (Beyond IntMap) and several normal slides following that. This happens to be in the org-mode format, but you can also write these outlines with Markdown.

If you’re used to working with WYSIWYG tools, this probably seems crazy. The connection between this outline and the generated slides is not nearly as clear as it would be in a tool like Powerpoint. So what’s the upside?

This is a fundamentally different model for editing slide documents. There’s a wonderful mental framework for thinking about different models like this in “ [When is one thing equal to some other thing?](http://www.math.harvard.edu/~mazur/preprints/when_is_one.pdf "www.math.harvard.edu")”, an article about abstract mathematics of all things. In particular, when we see different models for the same underlying idea, we need to pay attention to three things:

- What does each model shine a spotlight on?
- What does each model keep in the shadow?
- What does each model keep completely in the dark?

For WYSIWYG tools like Powerpoint, the spotlight shines on what the final document looks like. The outline of the slide deck as a whole is kept in the shadows—you can get a high-level overview of the entire presentation, but the overwhelming default is to work slide-by-slide. The shared structure of each slide, whether stylistic or semantic, is kept entirely in the dark. You can (and should) use structured styles in Powerpoint, but the tool doesn’t distinguish between these. A document that consistently uses styled headers and elements looks exactly the same as a document where each element is styled to look the same individually which looks the same as a document that started out using styled elements but then grew bits formatted in an ad-hoc way.

The outline-based approach I take with reveal.js is completely the opposite. The final result is kept in the shadow: I can preview what my slides will look like, but it takes an explicit action, and I don’t work on the preview directly. Instead, I primarily focus on the structure of my presentation as a whole. A similar dynamic happens for individual slides: the outline focuses on the semantics of individual elements (bullet points, text, code snippets, images) rather than what they look like. Detailed styling is done in a CSS file separate from the content of the presentation and is oriented based on structure (“headers look like this, code looks like that, screenshots look like…”) rather than a slide-by-slide basis.

The upside is that keeping my slides consistent is the default option. If I want to do something custom for one or two slides I can, but it requires a bit of extra effort—I’m only going to do it sparingly if it impacts my presentation or if I think it looks really cool.

![](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-033e672080aeddbe732bda1366b7cec9-pjlq)

The graph in the background of this slide was added mostly because I thought it was cool, and partly to be a visual reminder that we’re talking about graphs.

In Powerpoint, on the other hand, the default is making ad-hoc changes to individual slides. The result is that people without the right habits and discipline end up with presentations that are wildly inconsistent slide to slide, simply because they use Powerpoint the way the design of the tool pushes them to. Powerpoint is a bad tool not because it’s impossible to build good presentations with it but because building bad presentations is the path of least resistance.

Using reveal.js has a few other benefits specific to the kind of work I do:

- I can edit my presentation with Emacs
- I can keep track of versions with a version control system like Git
- It’s easy to add code snippets and math (with TeX)
- People can view my slides right from a browser or even their phones (example: [Radix Trees](http://jelv.is/talks/lambda-world-2018/slides.html "jelv.is"))

Would I recommend my exact workflow to anybody else?

If you are a programmer, I absolutely recommend it. The advantages of working with your slides in a structured way using normal programming tools are massive, and you’ll naturally end up with a simpler, more coherent presentation than you would with a Powerpoint-style tool. Using an outline format like org-mode or Markdown is way better than writing raw LaTeX for Beamer; the results with reveal.js look way better² and can still be turned into PDFs if needed.

Not a programmer? Probably not, then. You don’t need to do actual programming for your slides³, but you do need programming-adjacent tools like a solid text editor and version control system. If you want to go beyond a totally minimalist presentation, you’ll need some basic HTML and CSS knowledge. It’s easy once you get the hang of it, but there’s a non-trivial learning curve to get to that point.

But even if you aren’t a programmer, you should step back and think about what the tools you use encourage and what they discourage. Then you should either find different tools or start using the ones you have in a fundamentally different way.

footnotes

¹ WYSIWYG stands for “what you see is what you get”, software that lets you work directly with what is more or less the final document you are producing. WYSIWYG tools have major advantages—not least being intuitive and easy to pick up—but have the disadvantage of obscuring any structure behind the scenes of your document.

² The problem with Beamer is that almost all the templates for it are absolutely awful. The defaults are completely irredeemable and contribute to a lot of low-quality research presentations. Customizing Beamer enough to get something decent requires pretty non-trivial LaTeX work.

³ That said, I actually do generate some of the diagrams for my talks with code. I’ve found that using code to draw pictures of structures like graphs and trees makes it much easier to iterate on my presentation than drawing the same pictures by hand. If I had drawn a bunch of tree diagrams by hand and then came up with a clearer example, it would be too much work to redo the pictures; if I had code to generate the pictures instead, then redoing the example would only take a couple of minutes. This goes for all kinds of visualizations.

![](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-a1e5532f3497973682a9588265124013-pjlq)

I generated the tree diagrams in my talk with the Haskell [Diagrams](https://archives.haskell.org/projects.haskell.org/diagrams/ "archives.haskell.org") package. It took more work up-front, but saved me a lot of time when I was iterating on the contents of my talk.

If the deck was cluttered, filled with walls of text, or looked like four different people built it in four different styles, you probably stopped reading by slide three. ## Overview: Key features of presentation software

Presentation software helps users create visually appealing slide decks for effective presentations. Look for tools that balance ease of use, collaboration, and advanced features like AI generation and brand consistency. Here's what matters most for business pros:

| Presenter View/Notes | Keeps slides clean while giving you key points and timers. |
